descriptionChirho: A late feminine noun denoting spoil, plunder, or booty taken in warfare or raiding. Used consistently across all occurrences in Chronicles, Esther, Nehemiah, Daniel, and 1 Samuel to refer to material goods seized from defeated enemies. The separate clusters reflect only prepositional and conjunctive variation (bare noun, with beth-preposition, with lamed-preposition) but the core semantic meaning of captured war-goods remains identical throughout. All multilingual glosses converge on plunder/booty/spoil (arb: nahb/ghanimah, spa: botin/despojo, hin: lut, kor: yaktal-mul).
